headline: Bitcoin steady near $80,700 as markets wait for Wednesday’s Fed and Bank of Canada
summary: U.S. stocks closed higher ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision: the S&P 500 rose 0.6% to about 7,723 and the Nasdaq 1.2% to about 26,478 as AMD (+5.5%), Tesla (+4.0%) and Broadcom (+4.0%) led a third day of chip-led gains, while Boeing's roughly 10% slide kept the Dow flat; the TSX added 0.6% to about 36,171. In the evening, U.S. crude is about $100 (down 1.5%), gold is near $4,080 and the loonie has eased to about 71.2 U.S. cents, while Visa slipped in extended trading despite beating profit estimates. Crypto is steady but lagging: bitcoin is about $80,700 (up 0.7% over 24 hours, down 2.7% this week), ether about $2,345, total crypto value about $2.72 trillion and Fear & Greed a neutral 51, with the 10-year yield near 5.0% before Wednesday's Bank of Canada and Fed decisions.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin has hugged $80,000–$81,000 for two days while stocks rally, Fear & Greed is a neutral 51, total crypto value slipped about 1.9% over 24 hours, and options traders are still paying up for downside protection before Wednesday's Fed decision.

stocks.label: Risk-on
stocks.why: Chips, Tesla and big tech led a second straight up day and the VIX (Wall Street's fear gauge) fell about 5% to 17.5, though a 10-year yield near 5% and Wednesday's Fed, Bank of Canada and big-tech results keep the rally cautious.

drivers.title: AI money keeps flowing: Anthropic IPO filing, Nvidia's Meta stake, Broadcom financing
drivers.detail: Anthropic's IPO prospectus, filed Monday, showed $16.3 billion of first-half revenue and an $80.7 billion loss and lists more than $500 billion of compute commitments, per Yahoo Finance and HDFC Sky, while Nvidia said it will put $3 billion into Meta's share sale and banks plus Blackstone lined up roughly $60 billion-plus of debt for Broadcom's chip deal with Anthropic. Chipmakers extended Monday's rebound into the close (AMD +5.5%, Broadcom +4.0%, Nvidia +0.9% on our feed) while Meta fell 1.6% as investors weighed the dilution.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Up 0.7% over 24h but down 2.7% this week, at about $80,700 (down 4.0% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin slipped under $80,000 in Asian trading Monday as traders cut risk before Wednesday's Fed decision and has hovered within a few hundred dollars of it since, dipping to about $79,700 overnight and was around $80,700 in the evening, barely moving even as the Nasdaq rose more than 1%; it sits below its 50-day average, which some analysts read as near-term weakness, per CoinDesk. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold the coin for stock-market investors) took in about $110 million Monday, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinGabbar, after roughly $943 million of outflows over the prior three sessions per Farside, but Strategy said it made no bitcoin purchases in the week to Oct. 25, per Investing.com. A wallet tied to miner MARA also sent nearly 1,000 BTC to Galaxy Digital, per The Crypto Times, while futures markets price about a 90% chance the Fed holds rates. In options, the most-traded contract over the past day was a $72,000 put expiring Dec. 25, per ChainThink via KuCoin, showing continued demand for downside protection. Tech investor Jason Calacanis told followers Tuesday he expects bitcoin to fall to $57,000 within 12 months, while Galaxy argues it is a time to accumulate, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: Glassnode estimates ETF buyers and corporate treasuries bought, on average, between about $80,000 and $81,500, so bitcoin is sitting right around the price where many big holders break even; staying under it can prompt more selling. Monday's ETF inflow is a modest first sign that dip buyers are returning, but one day is not a trend.

outlook.bullCase: A calm Fed on Oct. 28, ETF inflows returning and a U.S.–Iran deal could lift it back above $82,000–$82,500 (Thursday's lost floor), putting $85,000–$87,000 back in view.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close below $79,000, more ETF outflows, a hawkish Fed or a U.S. strike on Iran could extend the slide toward $77,600 (Glassnode's estimate of the average holder's cost) and then $75,000.
outlook.watch: Whether it can close back above $80,000, whether ETF inflows continue, the Fed decision and Warsh press conference on Oct. 28, whether Strategy resumes buying (its results are Oct. 29), and about $11 billion of bitcoin options expiring Oct. 30.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Up 0.8% over 24h but down 4.3% this week, at about $2,345 (down 12.2% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether fell nearly 3% to just above $2,300 in Asian trading Monday, per CoinDesk, and is about $2,345 after Tuesday's U.S. close, up 1.4% over 24 hours. It is still under the $2,400 level that had supported it for about a week, and ether ETFs (over $1.1 billion out in October, their worst month this year, per Crypto Briefing) lost another roughly $89 million Monday, led by BlackRock's fund, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinGabbar, even as bitcoin ETFs drew money back in.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Climbing back above $2,400, with ETF outflows stopping, could open a move toward $2,500 and then about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: A break below $2,290 (Saturday's low) with continued ETF outflows and more forced selling could send it toward $2,150–$2,200, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,300 and $2,400 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: Bitway
crypto.move: Up about 44% over 24h on our feed (largely a rebound from a sharp dip about a day ago), at about $1.75; down 12% this week (up 43% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitway is the top 100's biggest 24-hour gainer, though much of that gain came from recovering a sharp dip, so most of that figure reflects a sharp dip about a day ago, with no specific news trigger we could find either way; it had already fallen about 25% on Oct. 15 when a hot U.S. inflation report hit crypto, and slid from above $2.60 to about $1.70 in the week to Oct. 24, per CoinMarketCap's update page. Trackers say the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, which makes sharp moves like this more likely, and about 101.6 million BTW (roughly 1% of the 10 billion total, about $175 million at today's price) is due to unlock on Nov. 2, per CryptoTicker. An unlock is when tokens held back for insiders or ecosystem funds become free to sell. Big swings in both directions are typical of a thinly traded token after a crash.
crypto.meaning: This is a high-risk token whose price can swing tens of percent in a day, with conflicting public data on how many tokens are actually circulating. Holders face more supply coming each month through 2030, and whether the Nov. 2 tranche goes to early backers (more likely to sell) or ecosystem pools is disputed between trackers.

outlook.bullCase: If the price holds above roughly $1.60 and the market absorbs the Nov. 2 unlock without heavy selling, a push back toward $2.00–$2.60 (mid-October levels) is possible.
outlook.bearCase: If large holders sell into the rebound or around the unlock, the price could fall back toward $1.20–$1.00, where it bottomed during the recent dip.
outlook.watch: Whether $1.60 holds, large wallet transfers to exchanges, trading volume, and price action around the Nov. 2 08:00 UTC unlock.

crypto.name: LayerZero
crypto.move: Up 2.6% over 24h but down 17.4% this week, at about $1.68 (up 3% over 30 days)
crypto.why: LayerZero runs a messaging system that lets apps send tokens and data between different blockchains, and ZRO is its token. It has bounced about 4% over the past 24 hours but is still down about 15% this week, and we found no fresh headline behind Monday's drop. It has been weak since an Oct. 20 token unlock (about 6% of supply), after which roughly 9.7 million ZRO was reportedly moved to big exchanges, per CoinMarketCap's AI news summary; an unlock is when tokens held back for insiders become free to sell. The project announced on Oct. 20 that its Zero mainnet and lzATLAS launch, which adds a buy-and-burn of ZRO funded by fees, is planned for Nov. 30, per TokenPost.
crypto.meaning: Recurring unlocks keep adding supply that early holders can sell, which has outweighed upgrade news so far this month. The Nov. 30 launch is the project's main potential catalyst, but a fee-funded burn only helps the price if the network earns meaningful fees.

outlook.bullCase: If selling from the unlock runs out and bitcoin steadies above $80,000, ZRO could bounce back toward $1.80–$2.00, where it traded last week.
outlook.bearCase: Continued exchange deposits from large wallets or a weaker crypto market after the Fed could push it below $1.60 toward about $1.40–$1.50.
outlook.watch: Large ZRO transfers to exchanges, whether $1.60 holds, the next monthly unlock date, and any update on the Nov. 30 Zero mainnet launch.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Up 1.4% over 24h and down 0.6% this week, at about $1.33 (down 12% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ripple, the company most closely tied to XRP, won final approval from the U.S. bank regulator (the OCC) for a national trust bank that will manage the reserves behind its RLUSD stablecoin and hold crypto for institutional clients, per CoinDesk. XRP rose about 1% on the news, per Investing.com, but is still around $1.30. Separately, Franklin Templeton last week put about $150 million more of its tokenized money-market fund onto the XRP Ledger, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: A federal bank charter gives Ripple's stablecoin and custody business more credibility with banks, but neither the charter nor tokenized funds require anyone to buy XRP, so the price link is indirect. XRP is still down about 15% over the past month, so this is a small bounce inside a larger slide.

outlook.bullCase: More tokenized-fund news and a steadier bitcoin above $80,000 could lift XRP back toward $1.40–$1.45.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin loses $80,000 again or the wider market turns risk-off after the Fed, XRP could slip back toward $1.20–$1.25.
outlook.watch: Whether XRP can hold gains on the bank-charter news, RLUSD growth, bitcoin's hold on $80,000, and the Oct. 28 Fed decision.

crypto.name: Quant
crypto.move: Down 1.6% over 24h but up 2.2% this week, at about $199 (down 41% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Quant makes software (its Overledger platform) that lets banks move tokenized money, meaning bank deposits recorded on a blockchain-style ledger, between different systems. The token rallied earlier this autumn on news that The Clearing House, the payments company owned by big U.S. banks, picked Quant's technology in late September for a project to settle tokenized deposits over its existing payment rails, with rollout targeted for the first half of 2027, though it has since given back much of that gain; seven big UK banks also made the first live customer payments with tokenized sterling on infrastructure Quant built, per CoinMarketCap. It jumped about 7% Monday without a fresh announcement we could find and is down about 1% over 24 hours after Tuesday's U.S. close, again with no announcement we could find.
crypto.meaning: QNT is trading on a real business story, bank adoption of tokenized money, rather than pure hype, but the actual rollout is still more than six months away and banks paying for software does not automatically mean demand for the token. After a roughly 23% gain in a month, much of the good news may already be in the price.

outlook.bullCase: More bank or payments-network announcements, or a broader recovery in crypto, could carry it past about $210–$225 on continued momentum.
outlook.bearCase: Profit-taking after a strong month, or a wider crypto sell-off if bitcoin stays below $80,000, could pull it back toward the $175–$180 area or lower.
outlook.watch: Any new partnership news from The Clearing House or UK banks, whether trading volume stays high, and bitcoin's direction around the Fed decision.

crypto.name: MemeCore
crypto.move: Up 13% over 24h and 38% this week, at about $1.07 (down 9% over 30 days)
crypto.why: MemeCore, a blockchain built around meme coins, was the biggest decliner among about 90 large coins tracked by TokenPost on Sunday morning, falling to about $0.92; it has since bounced to about $1.05, up about 10% over 24 hours and the biggest gainer in the top 100, with no specific trigger reported either way. The swings follow a choppy month: the token fell about 23% in the week to Oct. 19 after LayerZero and Stargate opened bridges letting holders move M to BNB Chain and Base, then bounced roughly 50%. On-chain investigator ZachXBT has previously accused insiders of manipulating the token's price, and a token unlock is due Nov. 1.
crypto.meaning: Moves of 20% in a day without clear news are typical of tokens where a few wallets hold much of the supply, so price can swing on a handful of trades. About 56 million new M tokens (roughly 2.8% of circulating supply, about $50 million, per CoinDesk) unlock on Nov. 1, which adds potential selling pressure.

outlook.bullCase: If the sell-off was one large holder exiting and the broader market steadies, it could rebound toward $1.05–$1.15, where it traded earlier this week.
outlook.bearCase: More large-wallet selling or selling ahead of the Nov. 1 unlock could push it toward $0.75–$0.80, its lows from mid-October.
outlook.watch: Large transfers to exchanges from top wallets, the Nov. 1 unlock, and whether the project explains the drop.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 5.1% over 24h and 3.7% this week, at about $1,298 (down 18% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and it noted an 8% drop in open interest Friday. After dipping below the $1,190–$1,230 support area, the price has bounced back to about $1,241 (up about 1% over 24 hours), inside the top of that zone.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and this week shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Up 0.3% over 24h but down 5.2% this week, at about $101 (down 17% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it slipped under $100 Saturday morning as bitcoin's break below $80,000 triggered forced selling across crypto, briefly tested $100 again in Asian trading Monday, and it is about $99.21 early Tuesday, just below that line.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or bitcoin staying below $80,000, could push SOL toward $90.
outlook.watch: Whether SOL regains $100, network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000 level, and Solana ETF flows.

Six of 11 sectors rose, with energy the laggard as oil eased, per AP, and October consumer confidence came in at 91.7, well above forecasts, per ActionForex.

stocks.name: Celestica
stocks.move: Jumped on Tuesday after Monday evening's results (about 9.7% higher at about C$380 around midday, per Baystreet.ca; our live feed does not track CLS)
stocks.why: Celestica, a Toronto-based company that builds servers, networking switches and other hardware for AI data centres, reported third-quarter revenue of $5.83 billion, up 83% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $3.30 a share, above its own guidance, per its filing. It raised its 2026 forecast to $21.0 billion of revenue and $11.55 a share (from $20.5 billion and $11.30), and gave a first 2027 outlook of $40 billion of revenue and $21.50 a share, nearly double this year. One soft spot: it cut its 2026 free-cash-flow forecast to $460 million from $600 million as it spends more to expand capacity.
stocks.meaning: The 2027 forecast says Celestica's biggest customers (large cloud companies) expect to keep spending heavily on AI hardware next year, a counterpoint to last week's worries about AI returns. The stock has already run up a lot on this story, so expectations are high and it is very sensitive to any sign that AI spending is slowing.

outlook.bullCase: If the premarket jump holds through the open and Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon confirm big AI spending plans this week, the stock could push toward fresh highs.
outlook.bearCase: If the broader AI-chip sell-off resumes, or investors focus on the lower cash-flow forecast and heavy spending, the opening pop could fade back toward Monday's close.
outlook.watch: Where it opens Tuesday in Toronto and New York, management's comments on customer concentration and capacity, and Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed down 1.6% at about $620, after Monday's 1.9% drop; down about 11% since last Wednesday
stocks.why: Nvidia said Tuesday it will put $3 billion into Meta's $35 billion share sale and expand work on Meta's Muse AI models, per Yahoo Finance. Meta launched a $35 billion share sale Monday to pay for AI data centres: about $22.5 billion of common stock sold through forward agreements and $12.5 billion of three-year mandatory convertible preferred shares (which turn into common stock later), plus a planned program of up to $60 billion of non-voting Class C shares starting in early 2027, per ZeroHedge and KuCoin News. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated interest in buying up to $5 billion. Shares rose before the bell, fell to about $629 after the open, recovered to about $648, before closing near the day's low at about $631. Last week's results beat forecasts, but the $135–$145 billion spending plan, roughly -$2.1 billion of free cash flow and a $9.9 billion legal charge sank the stock 7% Thursday. Meta priced the common-stock part at $625 a share (40 million shares, about $25 billion), with the convertibles set to turn into stock at about $734, per Bank of Vol.
stocks.meaning: Selling new shares spreads the company's profits over more stock (dilution), and the scale here is unusual for a company that was buying back shares. Chip-maker interest shows suppliers want to keep Meta spending, but it also feeds 'circular financing' worries, where AI buyers and sellers fund each other.

outlook.bullCase: If the offering is absorbed smoothly and investors refocus on 26% revenue growth, it could recover toward $680–$700.
outlook.bearCase: Pressure from new supply, rising credit-risk pricing (its five-year credit default swaps are about double August's level, per ZeroHedge) or weak results from other Big Tech spenders could push it below $630 toward $600.
outlook.watch: The offering's final pricing, whether $630 holds, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.move: Closed up 5.5% at about $560, building on Monday's 2.8% gain; about 15% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: AMD is among the day's biggest large-cap gainers as last week's AI-chip sell-off eases, helped by Anthropic's IPO filing and its large compute commitments, and it was named, along with Nvidia and Broadcom, as a possible buyer of up to $5 billion of Meta's new stock, per ZeroHedge and HDFC Sky. stocks.meaning: AMD has been one of the biggest AI winners of the past year, more than doubling from its low, so it swings hard when sentiment turns. Its own results on Nov. 3 are the next real test of whether AI chip demand is holding up.

outlook.bullCase: Strong Microsoft and Alphabet spending plans on Oct. 28 and solid guidance on Nov. 3 could lift it back toward $560–$600.
outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.
outlook.watch: Chip-sector moves, Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29, and AMD's Nov. 3 results.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed up 4.0% at about $407.50, after jumping 5.2% Monday to $391.62; still about 18% below its 52-week high of about $499
stocks.why: Barclays analyst Dan Levy upgraded Tesla to Overweight (a buy-type rating) and raised his target to $450 from $370, citing a possible combination with SpaceX (both companies have set up exploratory committees), a turnaround in the car business and faster robotaxi progress, per Investing.com. Sell ratings on the stock are now at their lowest share in about 11 years after BNP Paribas and CLSA dropped negative calls last week, and Latvia became the tenth EU country to approve Tesla's Full Self-Driving software.
stocks.meaning: Two days of gains are driven by deal hopes and analyst upgrades rather than new sales numbers, so the stock is pricing in a SpaceX tie-up that has not been agreed. That makes it sensitive to any headline about the merger talks in either direction.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete progress on a SpaceX combination or more upgrades could carry it toward Barclays' $450 target.
outlook.bearCase: If merger talk cools or big-tech earnings disappoint, it could give back the two-day jump toward the $370–$390 area it held last week.
outlook.watch: Any statement from the SpaceX and Tesla committees, big-tech results on Oct. 28–29, and whether it holds above Monday's $391.62 close.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.move: Closed up 4.0% at about $342.30; still about 31% below its 52-week high of $495
stocks.why: Broadcom is rising with other chipmakers after Anthropic's IPO filing, which named it among the suppliers in more than $500 billion of compute commitments, per HDFC Sky, and banks including Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley plus Blackstone lined up financing of roughly $60 billion or more for Anthropic's purchase of Broadcom-designed chips, per NewsBytes and earlier Bloomberg-sourced reports. It was also named as a possible buyer of Meta's new shares.
stocks.meaning: Broadcom designs custom AI chips for big customers, so a single deal of this size can shape its revenue for years; the financing removes some doubt about whether Anthropic can pay for it. The stock has fallen sharply from its highs on worries about how AI spending is funded, so it reacts strongly to news like this in either direction.

outlook.bullCase: If Big Tech's results on Oct. 28–29 confirm heavy AI spending and the Anthropic IPO goes smoothly, it could retake the $355–$375 range where it traded earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: If worries about debt-funded AI spending return or the chip rebound fades, it could slip back toward $320, Friday's low area.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above $335, Microsoft and Alphabet spending guidance on Oct. 28, Anthropic IPO pricing news, and the chip sector's next move.

stocks.name: Boeing
stocks.move: Fell roughly 10% on Tuesday after its earnings (about 9.5% lower at midday, per AP; our live feed does not track BA)
stocks.why: Boeing reported third-quarter revenue of $24.2 billion, up 4% on stronger defence and services, and a smaller core loss of $0.34 a share, but said it will deliver fewer than 500 737 jets this year, missing its 500-jet goal, per BigGo Finance's call summary. It also said getting 737 production steady at 47 a month will take into 2027, pushing back the cash recovery investors were counting on, though it set a goal of about $10 billion of free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) in 2029.
stocks.meaning: The drop reflects a delay, not a collapse: demand for jets is strong, but Boeing keeps taking longer than promised to build them. For holders, the stock now depends on hitting production targets month by month.

outlook.bullCase: Steady monthly delivery numbers and the long-term cash goal could help it stabilize and rebound from the $150 area.
outlook.bearCase: If the $150 area fails to hold and more analysts cut targets, it could slide toward the low $140s; it is already well below its September price near $190.
outlook.watch: Boeing's monthly delivery report in early November, analyst rating changes, and any FAA comment on production rates.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.move: Fell more than 1% in extended trading after results, per Reuters, after rising about 15% this year through Tuesday's close (our live feed does not track V)
stocks.why: Visa's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 13% to $12.1 billion and adjusted earnings rose 17% to $3.48 a share, ahead of the roughly $3.44 analysts expected, per AlphaStreet. Payments volume grew 9% and cross-border volume (spending outside a card's home country, a high-margin business) 14%. For fiscal 2027 it guided to revenue and earnings-per-share growth in the low double digits, per Reuters, and it raised its dividend 16% after buying back $4 billion of stock in the quarter.
stocks.meaning: The results show consumer spending, including travel, is holding up. The mild after-hours dip suggests the beat and a steady but unexciting 2027 outlook were largely priced in after October's roughly 11% run-up.

outlook.bullCase: If Wednesday's trading shakes off the after-hours dip and Mastercard's results confirm strong cross-border spending, the stock could retest its recent highs.
outlook.bearCase: If investors read the 2027 outlook as a slowdown, or UK card-fee legal claims and U.S. swipe-fee legislation gain traction, October's run-up could keep unwinding.
outlook.watch: Wednesday's regular-session reaction, Mastercard's results later this week, and any news on swipe-fee rules or the UK claims.
